newsitem.title: USA: CNG seeks to balance oil, gas production.
newsitem.headline: CNG seeks to balance oil, gas production.

text.p: Consolidated Natural Gas Co is seeking to balance its crude oil and natural gas production, said Pat Riley, president of CNG Producing Co, the utility holding company's producing arm.

The Pittsburgh-based company's production mix currently is about 85 percent natural gas and 15 percent oil, but crude production is expected to nearly double as a deepwater U.S. Gulf well comes on line in early 1997, Riley said on Thursday at the Rauscher, Pierce Refsnes Inc energy conference in Houston.

"In the long run, we'd like to change that to 50-50 oil and gas production," Riley said, adding that total production would be balanced by boosting crude production while keeping natural gas production steady.

The company expects total production to rise to 160 billion cubic feet equivalent (bcfe) in 1996 and 180 bcfe in 1997, up from 121 bcfe last year, said Riley, an Amoco Corp veteran signed on to head CNG Production.

The Neptune deepwater Gulf of Mexico play is expected to boost CNG's oil production to 7.5 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe) from about 3 million boe when it comes on line next year, he said. CNG has a 50 percent stake in Neptune, which is operated by Oryx Energy Co.

CNG Production plans to bid in the upcoming offshore federal lease sale in the Western Gulf production area, but also is seeking to increase its onshore drilling and is actively seeking acquisitions to boost reserves, he said.
